title: Canned Cowboy Candy (80/20 Jalapeno and Habanero)
description: Candied jalapenos for the water-bath canner, with 20% of the pepper weight swapped to habanero. Built on Ball's tested Candied Jalapenos recipe; garlic is in the tested recipe. Makes about 4 pint jars.

ingredients.note: 80% of the pepper weight. Sliced into 1/4 inch rings. Weigh, don't count.
20% of the pepper weight (about 13 oz). Sliced into 1/4 inch rings. Total peppers must stay exactly 4 lb.
must be labeled at least 5% acidity. Do not reduce.
canning or pickling salt keeps the syrup clear
sliced. This is the tested amount; don't add more.

steps: Put on disposable gloves before cutting any peppers and keep them on until the peppers are in the jars. Don't touch your face or eyes. Habanero oil burns much worse than jalapeno.
Turn on the range hood or open a window. Simmering hot peppers in vinegar puts out strong fumes that sting the eyes and throat.
Get the water-bath canner going. Heat 4 clean pint jars in simmering water until you need them; don't boil them. Wash the lids in warm soapy water and set them aside with the bands.
Weigh out 3.2 lb jalapenos and 0.8 lb habaneros (4 lb total). Slice both into 1/4 inch rings.
In a large saucepan, combine everything except the peppers: vinegar, sugar, salt, garlic, turmeric, cayenne, and mustard seeds. Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pepper rings. Turn the heat down to medium and simmer 15 minutes, until the jalapenos are dark green and have started to soak up the syrup.

Ladle the hot peppers and syrup into one hot jar at a time, leaving 1/2 inch headspace. Remove air bubbles, wipe the rim, center the lid, and screw the band on fingertip tight. Set the jar in the canner. Repeat until all the jars are filled.

Make sure the water covers the jars by 1 inch. Cover the canner and bring it to a rolling boil over medium-high heat. Once it reaches a rolling boil, process pint jars for 15 minutes (0 to 1,000 ft, which covers Elsah).
Turn off the heat, take off the canner lid, and let the jars sit 5 minutes. Lift them out without tilting and don't retighten loose bands.
Let the jars cool undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours. Check the seals: the lid shouldn't flex when you press the center. Refrigerate any jar that didn't seal and use it first.
Take off the bands, wash the jars, and label them with the name and date. Store in a cool, dry, dark place. The flavor gets better after a few weeks in storage.
source: Ball Candied Jalapenos (tested water-bath recipe): https://www.ballmasonjars.com/blog?cid=candied-jalapenos ; same recipe reprinted by UC Cooperative Extension: https://ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2024-11/404396.pdf . Pepper-swap rule: Ask Extension https://ask.extension.org/kb/faq.php?id=890923 and UC Master Food Preservers https://www.ucanr.edu/site/uc-master-food-preservers-inyo-and-mono-counties/pepper-substitutions . Altitude table: https://www.simplycanning.com/candied-jalapenos/ . Glove caution: NCHFP https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/pickling/pickled-hot-peppers . Adapted by Recipe Keeper for Joe, Oct 24, 2026.
notes:
Not yet made by Joe.
From the published Ball recipe, unchanged: 3 cups 5% vinegar, 4 cups sugar, 2 tsp salt, 6 cloves garlic, 2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 2 tsp mustard seeds, 4 lb peppers in 1/4 inch rings, 15 min simmer, 1/2 inch headspace, pint jars, 15 min water bath, 5 min rest in the canner, 12 to 24 hr cooling.
Recipe Keeper's changes: (1) The 80/20 split, 3.2 lb jalapeno and 0.8 lb habanero in place of 4 lb jalapeno. Ask Extension and UC Master Food Preservers both say you can swap one fresh pepper for another as long as the total weight stays the same. (2) Gloves and ventilation steps added. (3) Canning salt suggested for 'salt'.
Onion: NOT included. No tested candied-jalapeno recipe I found includes onion. Ball's tested version has garlic but no onion, and extension guidance says not to add low-acid vegetables to a tested pickle recipe. Onion in the jars would make this an untested recipe. Joe to decide: add onion when serving, or make a separate fridge-only batch.
Safety: Never cut the vinegar, use vinegar under 5%, cut the sugar, add more peppers or garlic, or add other vegetables (onion, bell pepper, pineapple). Use pint jars or smaller, never quarts. Altitude: 15 min covers 0 to 1,000 ft (Elsah is about 450 to 600 ft). At 1,001 to 3,000 ft it's 20 min, 3,001 to 6,000 ft 25 min, 6,001 to 8,000 ft 30 min.
Heat: habanero is far hotter than jalapeno (UC MFP puts Scotch bonnet at about 25 times jalapeno), so even 20% makes this much hotter than regular cowboy candy.
Leftover syrup (cowboy candy syrup): Ball doesn't say what to do with extra syrup. Keep any extra in the fridge. Don't can it by itself, because there's no tested process for that here.
Used in: Pulled Pork Wrap (freezer meal prep).

healthy: Jalapenos and habaneros are vegetables with vitamin C and other nutrients.
Eaten a spoonful at a time, so a serving is small.
Garlic and spices add flavor with no fat.
not_healthy: Candied in a heavy sugar syrup, so there's a lot of added sugar.
Very spicy, which can bother some stomachs.
